0.long_answer: Immunoglobulin E (IgE) is the immunoglobulin implicated in vernal keratoconjunctivitis. Although it is the least abundant isotype in the blood, IgE plays a central role in allergic responses. In vernal keratoconjunctivitis, allergens trigger an IgE-mediated reaction that leads to the activation of mast cells and an ensuing inflammatory cascade. This results in the characteristic symptoms of the condition, such as itching, redness, and other signs of severe ocular allergy. Elevated tear levels of IgE are often observed in patients with VKC and aid in its diagnosis and management.
